_what: Weight A/Bs for .github/workflows/experiments.yml. One entry per arm; every entry runs as its own job, in parallel, on its own runner.

_schema.slug: filename-safe id; names the artifact and the report
_schema.seeds: the sample, as lo-hi. Any size: the workflow cuts it into shards of `shard` seeds (default 128) and pools them
_schema.held: optional second block, disjoint from seeds; pooled with them (there is no early stopping to hold it out for any more)
_schema.title: one line for the generated note
_schema.context: why this arm, what it should show, and what it cannot -- the runner will not interpret the result for you
_schema.anchor: optional git ref: play against that revision's bot instead of HEAD with default weights
_schema.bot_ref: optional git ref: the challenger is that revision instead of HEAD. Cannot be combined with weights
_schema.openings: optional US=x,USSR=y; defaults to italy/austria whenever a ref is involved
_schema.compare_to: optional slug of another arm on the same seeds and opponent: collect reports the seed-by-seed paired difference. It must be dispatched TOGETHER with its target -- the pairing is collected within one run -- so `only=` both slugs in one call (`-f only=<target>,<arm>`). One dispatch per arm is the natural reading of this file and fails at plan time (2026-09-22: three dispatches, 15 s each)
_schema.shard: optional shard size in seeds (default 128, ~30-65 min on a runner)
_schema.logs: optional true: upload every game's INFO log

_sizing: 1024 seeds is the default for a question worth asking: +/-0.016 one-sided, against +/-0.045 at 128. The old 256-seed ceiling was one job's 6-hour limit, not a statistical choice; sharding removed it. Arms that share a seed block and an opponent are paired, so give every ablation of one question the same block and a compare_to.
_burst: The local queue existed because one machine runs one thing at a time; a runner per arm removes that. Prefer MORE ARMS AT FULL SIZE over fewer underpowered ones -- several 2026-09-12 experiments read +/-0.06 to +/-0.075 and could not settle what they were asked, purely because the box was the constraint.

experiments.title: refit at current main: weights fitted on 28adb67 vs bc5ef93
experiments.context: branch vp/refit-at-main. The weights were fitted on 598e4d1, two structural changes back, and weights fitted on the positions one bot reaches need not price the positions another reaches -- the standing argument for a refit, which survived the fresh block rather than being answered by it. The refit keeps the LEVEL (its matched_scale is measured against the shipped level, shipped rounded to 2.793), so this tests SHAPE. PRE-REGISTERED: paired lower bound above 0 means the refit ships; at or below 0 means the 598e4d1 weights stay and the staleness argument is spent, not merely unproven. Europe's in-sample R^2 FALLS 0.835 -> 0.576 on the refit while every other region holds or improves, so a loss here is the likely outcome and is worth knowing: it would say the linear model, not the sample, is what limits Europe. Cannot distinguish 'the refit is worse' from 'Europe needs a different functional form'.

experiments.context: The 1024-seed verdict the term has never had. `potential-round-on` read +0.021 [-0.009, +0.052] over 512 seeds against 07d553a (run 35531902621): not measured to help, not measured not to, at half the registry's own default for a question worth asking. At 1024 the interval roughly halves and separates +0.021 from zero if it is real. TWO THINGS CHANGED SINCE THAT READING and both matter. The opponent is bc5ef93, the strongest anchor, not 07d553a. And 15caae4 closed the gap where `_resolve_sandbox` never priced the potential at all, so events were mispriced against placements by the whole term (2.9075 VP on a 43 VP Fidel) -- the 512-seed reading was taken on a bot with events and placements on different scoring halves, and is NOT comparable to this one. PRE-REGISTERED: paired lower bound above 0 means the term earns its place and the refresh approximation is the next question; at or below 0 means it does not, at a sample size that can say so. Cannot separate the term from its `potential_refresh` round-level tables, which are on in both arms of the pair as they were in the 512-seed one.

experiments.title: hold option value: the term OFF vs bc5ef93, 1024 seeds
experiments.context: Step 1 of docs/notes/claude/2026-09-20-the-whole-hand-planner.md, ruling 3: a hold deserves option value for the flexibility of keeping it, and no measurement here says what it should be -- so `hold_option` ships at 0 and the hold-option-* arms price it over a small grid, the same shape as `vp_swing`, which is how that one was finally settled. The term is stated once in `hold_value`, so every live hold pricing reads it (Ask Not, the hand attacks, the Missile Envy and Aldrich picks); `value_as_held`, the planner's hold-slot price, delegates there and is what step 3 will read. The base half: the shipped bot, no premium, vs bc5ef93 -- the reference the three grid arms are paired against on identical machinery.

experiments.title: hold option value 0.25: a quarter of the card's Ops vs bc5ef93
experiments.context: The low end of the grid: a hold carries a quarter of its own Ops value on top of what it will be worth when played -- what a hold defers is the spending of its Ops, so the flexibility of choosing the moment is priced in those units. PRE-REGISTERED, read across the grid (025 / 05 / 10 paired against hold-option-base on one block): a peak anywhere with its paired lower bound above 0 means the flexibility is worth pricing and the peak value ships (gate first, then a MINOR bump); monotone rising through 1.0 means the peak is at or above 1.0 and the next question is a grid above it; every arm at or below 0 means ruling 3's term does not go into the live hold pricings at any size tested. Cannot separate 'the premium is wrong' from 'the premium belongs in the planner's hold-slot demand and not in the live hold terms' -- only the assignment planner (step 3) moves the latter.

experiments.title: hold option value 0.5: half the card's Ops vs bc5ef93
experiments.context: The middle of the grid: a hold carries half its own Ops value of flexibility. PRE-REGISTERED, read across the grid (025 / 05 / 10 paired against hold-option-base on one block): a peak anywhere with its paired lower bound above 0 means the flexibility is worth pricing and the peak value ships (gate first, then a MINOR bump); monotone rising through 1.0 means the peak is at or above 1.0 and the next question is a grid above it; every arm at or below 0 means ruling 3's term does not go into the live hold pricings at any size tested. This is where a peak is most likely to sit if keeping a card is worth about a small card's Ops. Cannot separate a peak at 0.5 from one at 0.4 or 0.6 -- three points is a direction and a bracket, not a fit.

experiments.title: hold option value 1.0: the card's whole Ops value again vs bc5ef93
experiments.context: The top of the grid: a held card carries as much again as its Ops value -- the flexibility priced at everything the card can buy. PRE-REGISTERED, read across the grid (025 / 05 / 10 paired against hold-option-base on one block): a peak anywhere with its paired lower bound above 0 means the flexibility is worth pricing and the peak value ships (gate first, then a MINOR bump); monotone rising through 1.0 means the peak is at or above 1.0 and the next question is a grid above it; every arm at or below 0 means ruling 3's term does not go into the live hold pricings at any size tested. A win here with 025 and 05 flat says the flexibility is worth pricing but this grid has not found the peak, and the next question is above 1.0. Cannot separate 'worth about 1.0' from 'worth more': 1.0 is the boundary of this grid.

experiments.context: PRE-REGISTERED, read paired against hand-assignment-base on one block: each turn's cards allocated by the solver -- one headline, R round units, the UN unit, ruling 4's space picks, holds as the remainder, a scoring card never held -- with ruling 1's two-solve space mix and ruling 5's scoring timing from the plan instead of +2 x action_round, and the survival DP untouched (ruling 2: subsumption is a later measured step). hand_assignment is a GATE, not a dial: any positive value is this bot. experiments.title: the assignment planner ON, leading only where it strictly prefers (hand_assignment 1.0) vs bc5ef93
experiments.context: PRE-REGISTERED, read paired against hand-lead-base on one block. The re-run of hand-assignment-on after its -0.240 was traced to the lead, not the allocation (docs/notes/claude/2026-09-23-the-planner-plays-its-hand-in-alphabetical-order.md). The solver's objective is flat almost everywhere: an ordinary card's price is the same in every round, and its hold price equals its play price at hold_option 0, so both the ORDER of rounds and WHICH cards are held were the solver's by-key tie-break. The lead now acts only on STRICT preferences, tested by re-solving with the candidate forced: a held card is demoted only if playing it lowers the plan's value; a headline leads only if it reaches the plan's value; the China Card, which the table cannot see, is never demoted. The scorer orders everything else exactly as shipped. Same solver, same rulings 1/4/5. Rule: paired lower bound above 0 means the planner's strict preferences beat per-card pricing and it ships (gate first, then the default flips); at or below 0 the gate stays shut. A reading below -0.10 is the size of a defect, not a verdict: find it before reading the number. Prior, stated before the number: close to 0 -- with play == hold the plan is strict mainly about the headline (headline price against play price), the space and UN units and scoring cards, so most action rounds rank exactly as shipped.

arms.title: a premium for holding the scoring card (1.25 vs 1.0, currently off)
arms.context: scoring_hand ships at 1.0, i.e. no premium at all, and the docs said 1.2 for long enough that nobody re-read it. The 2026-09-17 deck-walk fix (audit F3) moved 0.39 of occurrence mass per position out of bucket 3 and into bucket 2 -- a card in the draw pile is dealt THIS cycle, with certainty, not recycled into the next -- so the this-cycle mass of a card we do NOT hold rose 16% (2.42 -> 2.81 per position) while the mass of one we do hold did not move at all. Holding is therefore worth relatively less in mass terms than it was, and the only thing that could pay for the difference is the knob that is switched off. This arm asks whether choosing the MOMENT deserves a premium now that the deck math prices the timing correctly. A pass says 1.25 is free and the next arm brackets upward; a fail says holding is already fully paid for by bucket 1's certainty. It cannot separate 'holding is worth nothing' from 'holding is worth something the forecast already credits'.

arms.title: rival urgency at a quarter (0.25 vs 1.0), the far side of scoring-rival-half
arms.context: scoring_rival multiplies buckets 1+2 by (1 + r * P(the opponent holds it)), so at 1.0 a card they certainly hold doubles its own this-cycle urgency. F3 grew exactly that base by 16%, which means this knob's leverage went UP without anyone choosing that. scoring-rival-half (0.5) brackets the near side; this is the far side, so the pair reads as a direction rather than one point. Run both or neither: a single not-measurably-worse at 0.5 cannot distinguish 'the term is over-set' from 'the term does nothing', and 0.25 failing while 0.5 passes is what would locate the edge. Cannot calibrate r itself; three points on a curve is not a fit.
